primitives.name: Kinematic Style Attribute
primitives.verbatim_quote: The attributes are designed to capture the highlevel body movements of a player during the different phases of his shot, e.g., the jump and release.
primitives.assumptions: Player body pose is captured via broadcast video and annotated for movement style.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When body pose data is unavailable or mislabeled.

layer2.telemetry: Chi-squared divergence between made vs. missed shot attribute distributions.

primitives.name: Off-Balance Shot Frequency
primitives.verbatim_quote: We also present a case study for Stephen Curry, where we observe that Curry moves much more than the average player in all phases of his shot and he takes a higher proportion of off-balance shots compared to the average player.

Each shot is segmented into five temporal bins, and for each bin, 17 anatomical attributes are extracted. These include directional movement, limb usage, and balance. The chi-squared test is applied to compare these attribute distributions between made and missed shots. This creates a statistical signature of shooting style. The failure mode arises when attributes are not clearly distinguishable or when the sample size is insufficient for reliable chi-squared estimation. The dual nature of the approach lies in its ability to both characterize individual shooting styles (via descriptive attributes) and predict outcomes (via statistical divergence).
